acceptance: `evolve phase scout --cycle N` on a fixture cycle runs with the workspace, worktree and goal hash from that cycle's cycle-state.json (red: flag provided but not defined)
A cycle with no cycle-state.json, a missing worktree, or a live run lease exits 1 with the reason; --cycle together with a stdin request exits 10
`evolve compose --phases scout,triage --cycle N` runs both phases with the one derived request
fix: Add `--cycle N` (with `--project-root P`) to `evolve phase <name>` and `evolve compose`. When it is set, the command derives the PhaseRequest from runs/cycle-N/cycle-state.json (cycle, workspace, worktree and its base SHA, run id, goal hash) instead of reading stdin. It refuses with exit 1, naming the missing piece or the owning run, when the cycle has no state, its worktree is gone, or a live run lease holds it. Stdin stays the input when --cycle is absent; passing both is exit 10. One derivation function in phasecmd, which compose also calls, reads cycle-state.json with the existing core types and changes none of the orchestrator's writers. Document the flag for both commands in runtime-reference.md's operator commands.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: `evolve phase <name>` decodes a core.PhaseRequest JSON from stdin (internal/cli/phasecmd/phase.go:44-48), and `evolve compose --phases` reads the same envelope (cmd_compose.go:57-69). To rerun intent, scout, triage, tdd, build, audit, retro or debugger for a real cycle, the operator copies cycle, project_root, workspace, worktree, worktree_base_sha, run_id and goal_hash out of runs/cycle-N/cycle-state.json and the worktree list into hand-written JSON. A typo runs the phase against the wrong workspace, and nothing checks the request against the cycle.
title: `evolve phase <name>` and `evolve compose` take only a hand-written PhaseRequest on stdin; add `--cycle N` so a built-in phase reruns from the cycle's own state
